candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 20:1-13. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. 1 Cor 10:4; Heb 9:28.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On Moses' striking of the rock twice at Meribah (Num 20:11), Ephrem reads the doubled-strike as the proximate cause of Moses' exclusion from the land: the Lord had commanded that he speak to the rock, not strike it. The exegetical key, taken up by Paul (1 Cor 10:4 — 'that Rock was Christ'), is that Christ is struck once for the people's salvation; to strike him twice violates the typology of the once-for-all sacrifice (Heb 9:28, 10:10). Tewahedo christology cites Num 20:11 + 1 Cor 10:4 + Heb 9-10 as the canonical triple-witness that the Rock-Christ is smitten once and yields life-giving water forever.
